blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Recent advances in rectified flow-based image-to-3D generative models
have enabled high-fidelity 3D asset generation. Building on this,
a growing line of work has exploited these strong 3D priors for
training-free stylization, transferring visual attributes from a
reference image onto a generated 3D asset. However, existing methods
enforce an all-or-nothing paradigm: color and texture are transferred
jointly, with no mechanism to control them independently — a limitation we formalize as Disentangled 3D Stylization (Disen3D) . To address this, we propose DiDE , the first training-free framework for Disen3D . Key to our approach is the observation that the structured latent space of image-to-3D models is overcomplete with respect to texture: texture information occupies only a small subset of the style-significant channels, leaving a free subspace available for independent color encoding. DiDE exploits this via a channel partition mechanism that processes a content image, a texture reference, and a color reference through dedicated branches and composes both style signals interference-free at every self-attention layer, preserving content geometry throughout. Experiments on Disen3D-Bench, our newly collected multi-reference benchmark, show that DiDE consistently outperforms 2D and 3D stylization baselines in color fidelity, texture transfer, and content preservation.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Generative models for 3D asset creation have witnessed significant advancements Team (2024) ; Team (2025a) ; Xiang et al. (2025a) , facilitating their widespread adoption across diverse domains, including entertainment Xu et al. (2024) , robotics Ke et al. (2024) and healthcare Khader et al. (2023) .
In particular, recent rectified flow-based approaches Lipman et al. (2023) ; Liu et al. (2023) ; Team (2025b) , exemplified by TRELLIS Xiang et al. (2025a) ; Xiang et al. (2025b) , have demonstrated the ability to generate high-fidelity 3D objects by jointly modeling sparse structural representations and appearance features within a unified latent space, while explicitly disentangling geometric structures from appearance attributes.
Beyond 3D asset generation, a growing line of work has extended generative models to support 3D stylization Hu et al. (2026) ; Qu et al. (2025) ; Sun et al. (2026) — the task of transferring stylistic attributes from a reference image onto a generated 3D asset. By conditioning generation on a style reference, these methods allow the produced asset to inherit visual properties such as surface material, color palette, and structural texture, while remaining semantically aligned with a content image.
This capability carries significant practical value: a single base geometry can be re-stylized for different artistic contexts, production pipelines, or brand identities without requiring manual re-authoring. Although existing stylized 3D generation methods Qu et al. (2025) ; Sun et al. (2026) have achieved promising results, they still exhibit a critical limitation: style attributes (such as texture and color) cannot be controlled independently, which severely restricts artistic freedom in practice.

blocks.en:
In practice, content creators rarely want to adopt a single reference style. Instead, they often wish to selectively borrow specific components while preserving the core of their own artistic vision Epstein et al. (2023) ; Hertzmann (2022) . Color palettes play an essential role in this process: they are carefully designed to convey specific emotions or maintain brand consistency, and a creator may wish to preserve their own color scheme while borrowing surface texture from a reference. Equally, one might want to adopt the rough, weathered texture of aged stone from one reference while keeping the warm tones of an entirely different palette. These two attributes — color and texture — are visually and semantically distinct, yet current 3D stylization approaches Hu et al. (2026) ; Qu et al. (2025) enforce an all-or-nothing paradigm: applying a reference style requires accepting all its visual attributes simultaneously, which severely restricts artistic freedom and practical applicability.
To the best of our knowledge, only one prior work addresses disentangled stylization in 2D Qin et al. (2025) , yet it cannot be generalized to 3D, as style embeddings from separate references cannot simply be composed in 3D latent space. This leaves the problem of fine-grained, decoupled 3D stylization entirely open.

blocks.en:
To address these limitations, we introduce Disentangled 3D Stylization ( Disen3D ), which aims to decompose reference styles into independently controllable color and texture attributes, enabling artists to selectively transfer specific style elements while preserving content geometry.
We further propose Direct Injection with color-texture DEcoupling ( DiDE ), the first training-free framework for this task, which takes three inputs — a content image, a texture reference, and a color reference — processed through dedicated branches. To achieve this, We build on prior findings Qu et al. (2025) showing that feature channels of image-to-3D models Xiang et al. (2025b) can be decomposed into style- and content-significant subsets, with one branch dedicated to style and another to content. However, directly extending this framework with an additional branch for color is non-trivial: combining two style branches through the same attention pathway leads to feature interference, making disentangled control of texture and color difficult.
To address this problem, we further show that texture information occupies only a subset of the style-significant channels, leaving additional feature capacity available for encoding an independent color attribute. We allocate those informative channels from the texture branch, while populating the remaining free channels with color features from a separate color reference branch. Finally, this partition is applied at every self-attention layer of the texture generation stage, enabling composable, interference-free injection of texture and color while preserving full 3D consistency.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
3D Generative Models. Two dominant paradigms have been established for high-quality 3D asset generation.
The first focuses on distilling useful priors from pretrained 2D generative models into feed-forward 3D reconstruction algorithms.
They either fine-tune 2D models to synthesize multi-view images Shi et al. (2024) ; Shriram et al. (2025) ; Yu et al. (2025) , which are further reconstructed into 3D assets via techniques such as 3D Gaussian splatting Kerbl et al. (2023) ;
or directly guides 3D optimization through gradient signals from 2D diffusion models Poole et al. (2023) .
Despite their effectiveness, they lack an explicit latent 3D space to achieve fine-grained structural control.
To overcome this limitation, the second paradigm pursues unified native 3D generative models trained from scratch.
Inspired by the remarkable success of diffusion models in visual synthesis Ho et al. (2020) ; Khachatryan et al. (2023) ; Rombach et al. (2022) , recent methods Cheng et al. (2023) ; Ren et al. (2024) ; Vahdat et al. (2022) ; Zeng et al. (2024) learn compact latent representations and perform generation within this compressed latent space, significantly advancing 3D generative modeling.
Benefiting from large-scale 3D datasets Deitke et al. (2023a) ; Deitke et al. (2023b) , modern 3D foundation models Chen et al. (2025b) ; Hong et al. (2024) ; Li et al. (2025) ; Team (2025b) have been developed to capture strong geometric priors, enabling not only high-quality generation across diverse object categories but also various downstream applications Du et al. (2025) ; Hu et al. (2024) .
However, most existing native 3D generators are restricted to either explicit representations
or implicit formulations.
TRELLIS Xiang et al. (2025b) addresses this constraint by introducing a Structured Latent Representation (SLAT) that supports flexible multi-format 3D generation, whose versatility we inherit to accommodate diverse 3D modalities in our framework.
Although these 3D foundation models exhibit strong generalization abilities, they mainly generate samples from a learned data distribution and lack dedicated mechanisms for
example-driven control.
In this work, we leverage the powerful priors from the 3D foundation model TRELLIS Xiang et al. (2025b) and introduce a decoupled personalization framework.
Our approach enables flexible adaptation of both geometry and appearance, while fully retaining the high-quality generative capacity of the underlying models.

blocks.en:
Controllable 3D Generation. Recent methods have been developed to enable image-guided control for 3D generation Dong et al. (2024) ; Gao et al. (2025) ; Huang et al. (2024) ; Wang et al. (2024) ; Xu et al. (2023) .
Among these, some approaches inject explicit shape priors to regulate the geometric attributes of synthesized 3D content.
In parallel, another line of work unifies the stylistic appearance of generated objects by leveraging reference images Richardson et al. (2023) ; Song et al. (2024) ; Xie et al. (2024) ; Yeh et al. (2024) .
However, such style-guided 3D generation pipelines typically require users to provide predefined 3D geometry such as meshes, and enforce fixed geometric structures throughout generation to maintain spatial consistency.
This strong restriction confines their controllability to texture style only, while leaving geometric style—another critical dimension of 3D asset customization—unchanged and fully uncontrollable.
In this work, we employ TRELLIS as our backbone model, taking advantage of its expressive 3D latent representations that comprehensively encode both geometric structure and textural appearance.
Built on these latent features, we achieve zero-shot style-guided 3D generation that supports simultaneous control over both texture and geometric style.

blocks.en:
Image-based 3D Stylization. Given a style reference input and a target content shape, 3D stylization is defined as the task of distilling stylistic patterns from the reference and transferring these patterns to the target geometry to synthesize stylistically aligned 3D assets. This problem has been investigated across diverse 3D representation frameworks, including explicit meshes Hertz et al. (2020) ; Höllein et al. (2022) ; Hu et al. (2024) , neural implicit fields, and Gaussian splatting Huang et al. (2025) ; Huang et al. (2022) .
To enhance generalizability, a prominent line of recent work Chen et al. (2025a) ; Dong et al. (2024) ; Xie et al. (2024) harnesses powerful 2D priors from large-scale image diffusion models Rombach et al. (2022) for 3D stylization. Concurrently, StyleSculptor Qu et al. (2025) leverages strong 3D priors Xiang et al. (2025b) to achieve view-consistent stylization.
However, all these approaches share a critical limitation: contemporary 3D stylization methods Hu et al. (2026) ; Qu et al. (2025) enforce an all-or-nothing paradigm, where adopting a reference style necessitates the simultaneous incorporation of all its visual attributes. This inherent constraint severely limits
the methods’ practical utility in real-world content creation scenarios.

blocks.en: 3 Methods
blocks.zh: 3个 方法

blocks.en:
To address the Disen3D problem, we propose a disentangled 3D style transfer framework DiDE built upon the TRELLIS backbone.
Given a content image I c ​ n ​ t I_{cnt} , a texture reference I t ​ x ​ u I_{txu} , and a color reference I c ​ o ​ l I_{col} , our goal is to generate a 3D asset that (i) preserves the geometric structure of I c ​ n ​ t I_{cnt} , (ii) inherits texture from I t ​ x ​ u I_{txu} , and (iii) adopts color from I c ​ o ​ l I_{col} , while maintaining cross-view consistency. Unlike conventional 2D style transfer, our approach performs disentangled style modeling in the 3D latent space and injects style during rectified flow-based refinement.

blocks.en: 3.1 Preliminaries
blocks.zh: 3.1 初步情况

blocks.en:
TRELLIS Xiang et al. (2025b) is a foundation model for conditional 3D asset generation that synthesizes assets in multiple representations (e.g., NeRF, 3DGS, mesh) from text or image inputs.
It adopts a two-stage rectified flow framework to progressively transform noise into structured 3D representations: Stage I predicts a sparse geometric structure, and Stage II refines per-voxel latent features for texture and material details.

它采用了一个两阶段修正的流程框架,逐步将噪音转化为结构化的三维表示: 第一阶段预测的是稀疏的几何结构,第二阶段则精炼每伏牛潜伏的特征,用于纹理和材料细节.

blocks.en: 3.2 Overcompleteness of the TRELLIS Feature Space
blocks.zh: 3.2 TRELLIS特性空间的过度完成

blocks.en:
StyleSculptor Qu et al. (2025) showed that TRELLIS feature channels can be decomposed into style and content-relevant subsets via patch-wise variance. However, their formulation assumes a single style reference. In our setting, texture and color must be injected independently into the same style branch, which can lead to feature interference. We therefore investigate whether the style-significant channels are overcomplete, asking whether all of them are actually required to faithfully encode texture. We conduct a channel ablation experiment in which we progressively reduce the number of channels used for texture injection at every DiT block of TRELLIS stage II, retaining only the top-k highest-variance channels from the style branch of Stage II. For each value of k, we generate outputs across the full set of style references from StyleSculptor Qu et al. (2025) using a fixed content image, render a single view, and measure DINOv2 cosine similarity between the mean patch features of the rendered output and the corresponding style reference image.
As shown in Fig. 3 , DINOv2 texture similarity is ≈ 0.6125 \approx 0.6125 when only a small fraction of channels is retained, rises to ≈ 0.625 \approx 0.625 – 0.63 0.63 once more than 25 % 25\% of the channels are retained, and remains within this range up to 100 % 100\% .
To further support this finding, we conduct a PCA reconstruction analysis (see appendix), confirming the low intrinsic dimensionality of texture within the TRELLIS feature space, and validating that style-significant channels contain a large free subspace that can be independently allocated to a second style attribute.

样式浮雕 Qu et al. (2025)显示,TRELLIS特征通道可以通过修补差异分解为样式和内容相关子集. 然而,其措辞采用了单一的风格。 在我们的设置中,纹理和颜色必须独立地注入到同一个样式分支,这会导致特征干扰. 因此,我们调查风格重要频道是否过于完整,询问是否要求所有频道都忠实地编码纹理。 我们进行了一个信道减速试验,在试验中我们逐步减少TRELLIS第二阶段每个DiT区块的纹理注射所用的信道数量,只保留第二阶段风格分支的顶-k最高变速信道. 对于 k 的每个值, 我们从 StyleSculptor Qu et al 生成整个一组样式引用的输出 。 (2025)使用固定的内容图像,渲染一个单一视图,并测量得到输出的平均补丁特征与相应的样式参考图像之间的DINOv2余弦相似度.

blocks.en: Color Reference. Our method supports two types of color reference inputs: reference images , common in style transfer applications, and color palettes , widely used in multimedia and design workflows. Both are processed to isolate color information from texture structure before encoding.
blocks.zh: 颜色参考. 我们的方法支持两种类型的颜色参考输入: 参考图像,常见于样式传输应用程序,和色彩调色板,广泛用于多媒体和设计工作流程. 两者都经过处理,在编码前将颜色信息从纹理结构中分离出来.

blocks.en: When a reference image is used as the color reference, we extract its low-frequency components via a Fourier transform while suppressing high-frequency signals. Intuitively, high-frequency components primarily encode textural details (e.g., edges and fine patterns), whereas low-frequency components capture global color distributions. By filtering out high-frequency signals, our method enforces a structure-invariant color conditioning, thereby improving the disentanglement between color and texture.

representation. This fused output is then injected into the content
branch, overwriting its self-attention output before the residual update.

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: We conduct extensive experiments to validate three core claims of DiDE : (i) effective disentanglement of color and texture in the generated 3D assets, (ii) faithful preservation of the content geometry, and (iii) competitive style fidelity against existing methods. Since no prior benchmark addresses the Disen3D setting, we introduce Disen3D-Bench and compare against representative 2D and 3D stylization baselines.
blocks.zh: 我们进行了广泛的实验,以验证DiDE的三项核心主张:(一) 在生成的3D资产中有效分解颜色和纹理,(二) 忠实地保存内容几何,(三) 与现有方法相抗衡的风格忠诚。 由于先前的基准没有针对Disen3D设置,我们引入Disen3D-Bench,并与代表性的2D和3D分层化基线进行比较.

blocks.en: Datasets. We collected 37 images to form a novel multi-image style transfer dataset named Disen3D-Bench for the Disen3D setup. These images include 10 content images, 12 texture reference images, and 15 palette images. The content images and texture reference images were selected from Stylesculptor Qu et al. (2025) and Morph3D Sun et al. (2026) , and each palette image contains 3-5 different colors. These image combinations generate 1,800 3D assets for subsequent evaluation.

blocks.en:
Qualitative Results. In our evaluation of generation quality, visual results are presented in Fig. 5 .
For SADis, the method exhibits subpar object detail preservation, while introducing redundant textures and color artifacts in the background region. After 3D rendering, the reconstructed textures and colors also fail to align closely with the reference images.
For StyleSculptor, the model fails to achieve full disentanglement of texture and color. The generated 3D assets exhibit a mixed color distribution derived from both reference images; furthermore, the results often suffer from style bias, tending to favor either the texture reference or the color reference rather than achieving balanced, independent control over both attributes.
Regarding MorphAny3D, its Morphing Cross-Attention mechanism causes the colors and styles inherent in the content image to exert a significant influence on the final generation result. Additionally, the method generates spurious colors that are not present in the provided color palette images.
In contrast, our DiDE enables precise decoupling of texture structure and color attributes. For instance, we can accurately align the cutout structure of the texture reference with the target color— a capability not achievable by other baseline methods. Simultaneously, our method DiDE ensures that the generated 3D asset remains consistent with the content image, free from distortions, flips, or other visual artifacts.

定性结果. 在我们对生成质量的评价中,视觉结果见图5。
对于SADIS,该方法显示子化对象细节保存,同时在背景区域引入冗余纹理和彩色文物. 3D渲染后,重建的纹理和颜色也未能与参考图像紧密一致.
对于StyleSculptor来说,模型未能实现纹理和颜色的完全分解. 生成的3D资产呈现出来自两个参考图像的混合色彩分布;此外,结果往往带有风格偏差,倾向于倾向于纹理参考或色彩参考,而不是实现对两个属性的平衡,独立控制.
关于MorphAny3D,它的Morphing Cross-Attention机制使得内容图像固有的颜色和风格对最终生成结果产生了重大影响. 此外,该方法还生成在所提供的色调图像中没有的虚假颜色。
相比之下,我们的DiDE能够精确解析纹理结构和颜色属性. 例如,我们可以精确地将纹理参考物的剪切结构与目标颜色——这种能力是其他基线方法无法实现的。 同时,我们的方法DiDE确保生成的3D资产与内容图像保持一致,没有扭曲、翻转或其他视觉文物。

Quantitative Results. Table 1 reports the full results. DiDE achieves
the best CLIP-I score (0.75), indicating superior semantic alignment with the
content image. For Geometry, DiDE achieves the lowest Chamfer distance (15.38) and Hausdorff distance (7.87) under the reported scaling. Compared with the strongest baseline, StyleSculptor, DiDE reduces the two distances by approximately 14.1% and 6.1%, respectively. Although SADis achieves a Chamfer distance comparable to those of StyleSculptor and DiDE , its substantially higher Hausdorff distance indicates much larger worst-case local geometric deviations that are not fully captured by the averaged Chamfer distance. These complementary metrics demonstrate that DiDE better preserves both overall surface structure and local geometry during stylization.
For color fidelity, DiDE leads on C-Hist (0.87) and by a
large margin on VLM color accuracy (70.94 vs. 40.05 for the next best method),
confirming faithful and disentangled color transfer. While MorphAny3D and SADis
yield slightly better MS-SWD scores (18.31 and 18.38 vs. 20.40), this comes at
the cost of degraded texture structure, as reflected in their lower SSIM scores.
For texture quality, DiDE attains the highest SSIM (125.19) and VLM
texture accuracy (30.72 vs. 23.22 for StyleSculptor), demonstrating superior
structural preservation and texture fidelity. LPIPS scores are comparable across
all methods (0.65–0.69), suggesting similar levels of perceptual distortion
relative to the content image.

blocks.en: Effect of Branch Preprocessing. We ablate the two key preprocessing components of DiDE — grayscale conversion of the texture reference and Voronoi tessellation of the color palette — by removing each in turn while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged. As shown in Fig. 6 , removing grayscale conversion leaves residual color information in the texture branch, introducing undesired color interference in the generated output. Removing Voronoi tessellation causes color leakage, producing colors that deviate from the reference palette.
blocks.zh: 预处理处的效果。 我们放弃了DiDE的两个关键预处理组件——纹理参考物的灰度转换和彩色调色板的Voronoi脱落——方法是在保持管道其余部分不变的情况下逐个去掉。 如图6所示,去除灰度转换会在纹理分支中留下剩余颜色信息,对生成的输出引入不受欢迎的颜色干扰. 删除 Voronoi 调色板会导致颜色渗漏,产生偏离参考调色板的颜色.

blocks.en: Model Adaptability. To verify the generalizability of DiDE beyond the base TRELLIS backbone, we apply it to TRELLIS.2 Xiang et al. (2025a) , which extends TRELLIS with a three-stage pipeline where texture and color features are processed in separate stages. As illustrated in Fig. 7 , DiDE maintains robust and consistent disentanglement performance on TRELLIS.2, confirming that our channel partition mechanism transfers across model variants. The natural stage-wise separation in TRELLIS.2 further aligns with our texture-color decoupling design, making the adaptation straightforward.

blocks.en: Channel Selection. In DiDE , channel variance is computed from the texture branch to determine the channel partition. To assess the sensitivity of this design choice, we ablate by computing variance from the color branch instead, swapping which branch drives the partition. As shown in Fig. 8 , both settings achieve consistent texture-color disentanglement, with only minor differences in color saturation. This robustness to the choice of variance source corroborates our earlier finding (Sec. 3.2 ) that the latent feature space is overcomplete, with texture and color information redundantly distributed across channels regardless of which branch is used for estimation. We use texture-branch variance as default since it produces marginally more faithful color rendition in practice.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
This work addresses a fundamental limitation in existing 3D stylization methods: the inability to independently control distinct stylistic attributes such as color and texture. We formalize this gap as Disentangled 3D Stylization ( Disen3D ) and propose Direct Injection with color-texture DEcoupling ( DiDE ), the first training-free framework to address it. DiDE decouples texture and color by processing each reference through a dedicated branch with tailored preprocessing and composes them via a channel partition mechanism injected into the
self-attention layers of a pretrained image-to-3D model, preserving content geometry throughout. Extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations on Disen3D-Bench confirm that DiDE outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in disentangled color and texture control. We hope this work opens the door to finer-grained artistic control in 3D content creation and inspires future research on multi-attribute style disentanglement.
blocks.zh:
这项工作解决了现有3D分层化方法中的一个基本限制:无法独立控制不同的分层特征,如颜色和纹理. 我们把这个差距正式化为Distentrongled 3D Stylization(Disen3D),并提议用彩色-纹理DEcoupling(DiDE)进行直接注射,这是第一个解决这个问题的无训练框架. DiDE 脱钩纹理和颜色,通过专用分支处理每个参考物,并配备定制的预处理器,通过注入到该参考物的通道分区机制来编曲
预加训练的图像到3D模型的自留层,在整个图中保存内容几何. 对Disen3D-Bench进行广泛的定性和定量评价,证实DiDE在分散的颜色和纹理控制上超过了最先进的基线. 我们希望这部作品打开了3D内容创作中精细刻画的艺术控制之门,并激励未来对多属性风格分散的研究.

Limitations. While DiDE effectively mitigates detail attenuation and enhances fine-grained texture fidelity for training-free disentangled 3D stylization, it has several limitations: the framework is only validated on rectified flow-matching based native 3D diffusion models (the TRELLIS/TRELLIS.2 family) and has not been tested for generalization to other mainstream 3D generation paradigms, including voxel-based models, signed distance field (SDF) generators, 3D Gaussian splatting diffusion pipelines, and knowledge distillation-based image-to-3D methods.
Furthermore, although the computational overhead is negligible, the low-noise restart refinement step adds mild extra inference operations, restricting direct deployment on extremely memory-constrained edge devices.
Finally, DiDE focuses on color-texture decoupling and texture enhancement without a dedicated geometric refinement module, so the geometric quality of the generated 3D assets is inherently dependent on the geometric reconstruction capability of the underlying pre-trained 3D foundation model;
and the current design only supports independent control of color and texture, without extending to multi-attribute disentanglement (e.g., material, lighting, geometric style), which limits its flexibility for complex artistic creation.
blocks.zh:
限制。 虽然DiDE有效缓解了细节的衰减,并加强了精细的纹理忠贞度,用于无训练的脱落3D结构化,但它有多个局限性:这个框架只在纠正流配原生3D传播模型(TRELLIS/TRELLIS.2家族)上验证过,并且还没有被测试通化到其他主流3D生成范式,包括Voxel型模型,签名的距离场(SDF)发电机,3D高斯电镀扩散管道,以及基于知识的蒸馏成像到3D方法.
此外,虽然计算间接费用可以忽略不计,但低噪声重启完善步骤增加了轻度推断操作,限制了在极受内存限制的边缘设备上直接部署.
最后,DiDE专注于色彩-纹理脱钩和纹理增强,没有专用的几何精细化模块,因此生成的3D资产的几何质量本质上依赖于基础预训练的3D基础模型的几何重建能力;
而目前的设计只支持对颜色和纹理的独立控制,而不延伸至多分配的分散(如材料,照明,几何风格),这限制了其对复杂艺术创作的灵活性.

blocks.en: Broader Impacts. DiDE advances controllable 3D content creation and delivers widespread practical value by enabling training-free, disentangled color-texture control for 3D stylization, which drastically lowers the technical barrier and production cost for generating high-fidelity and customizable 3D assets, benefiting diverse industries and scenarios including game development, film and television virtual production, industrial design, cultural heritage digitization, robotic perception, and metaverse content construction, empowering both professional creators and non-expert users to flexibly customize 3D assets with independent style control, improving creative efficiency and diversifying content supply; on the other hand, the strong detail-preserving and high-fidelity texture transfer capability of DiDE introduces potential intellectual property and ethical risks, as the model could be misused for unauthorized duplication, counterfeiting, or commercial exploitation of copyrighted objects, branded products, real-world artifacts, or cultural heritage items without permission, and to address such risks, we advocate for the responsible deployment of the technology, enforcing content authentication for generated assets, establishing clear usage norms and legal compliance guidelines, and promoting ethical adoption across industries to ensure that DiDE creates public value while minimizing harms from misuse.

Ethical Statement. We acknowledge the potential ethical implications associated with generative image-to-3D technologies, including risks related to privacy, impersonation, and misuse of synthetic 3D assets. All models used in this work are trained on publicly available datasets and follow the usage policies of those datasets.
To promote transparency and responsible research, we will release the implementation details necessary to reproduce our results. We encourage researchers and practitioners to use DiDE responsibly and to consider the broader societal implications when deploying image-to-3D synthesis .

Appendix C Hyperparameter visualization
blocks.zh: 附录C 超参数可视化

blocks.en:
We further analyze the influence of the hyperparameter λ \lambda in Equ. 7 on disentangled generation quality. Specifically, λ \lambda controls the contribution of the color branch during feature fusion. We evaluate five settings, λ ∈ 0.5 , 1.0 , 1.2 , 1.5 , 2.0 \lambda\in{0.5,1.0,1.2,1.5,2.0} , and visualize the corresponding results in Fig. 10 .
As shown in the figure, smaller values of λ \lambda (e.g., 0.5 0.5 ) lead to insufficient color guidance, causing the generated 3D assets to inherit excessive appearance information from the texture branch. In contrast, excessively large values of λ \lambda (e.g., 1.5 1.5 or 2.0 2.0 ) overemphasize color features, which weakens texture fidelity and introduces structural inconsistencies.
We observe that λ = 1.2 \lambda=1.2 achieves the best balance between texture preservation and color controllability. Under this setting, the generated results faithfully maintain the structural patterns from the texture reference while accurately matching the target color distribution, leading to the most visually coherent disentangled generation results.

we provide additional qualitative results to further demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our method across diverse texture and color references. As shown in Fig. 12 , our method consistently achieves effective disentanglement between texture structure and color attributes under various challenging scenarios.
Specifically, the generated 3D assets faithfully preserve the structural patterns and geometric details from the texture reference while accurately matching the target color distribution from the color reference image. blocks.en:
To further validate the overcompleteness claim of Sec. 3.2 , we perform a PCA analysis on the style-significant channels of the TRELLIS Stage II features. We project the style branch features onto an increasing number of principal components and measure DINOv2 cosine similarity between the rendered output and the texture reference.
As shown in Fig. 13 , similarity stabilizes after retaining as few as 10 principal components, despite the full channel dimensionality being much larger. This confirms that texture occupies an extremely low-dimensional subspace, leaving the majority of the feature space free to be independently repurposed for color encoding — directly motivating our channel partition design.
blocks.zh:
为了进一步证实第3.2节的过份完整的说法,我们对TRELLIS第二阶段特征的风格重要渠道进行了常设仲裁法院的分析。 我们将样式分支特征投射到越来越多的主要组件上,并测量输出和纹理参考物之间的DINOv2余弦相似性。
如图13所示,相似性在保留了多达10个主要组件之后稳定下来,尽管整个信道的维度要大得多。 这证实了纹理占据了极低维的子空间,使得大部分的特征空间可以自由独立地重新用于色彩编码——直接激发了我们的频道分区设计.
